questions.question: Which of the following is NOT acceptable emergency equipment?

options.text: Three red reflective triangles
Six fuses
Three liquid burning flares
Four yellow squares

questions.correctAnswerText: Four yellow squares
questions.explanation: You must show emergency equipment during the vehicle inspection test. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles OR six fuses OR three liquid burning flares, and a properly charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: If driving a school bus, your four-way flashers should:

options.text: Be turned on before crossing railroad tracks.
Never be used.
Only be used after crossing railroad tracks.
Only be used near railroad tracks if a train is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be turned on before crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: When driving a school bus, turn on your four-way flashers as you approach and cross railroad tracks. Turn them off after your entire vehicle has crossed the tracks.

questions.question: When boarding a school bus, students should:

options.text: Line up single-file.
Line up in pairs.
Not use the handrail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Line up single-file.
questions.explanation: Students should board slowly in a single-file line. They should use the handrail for safety.

questions.question: If you need to back into an alley, you should first:

options.text: Drive directly into the alley parking space.
Turn right to position yourself in front of the alley.
Drive past the alley and stop with your vehicle perpendicular to the edge.
Drive past the alley and stop with your vehicle parallel to the edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive past the alley and stop with your vehicle parallel to the edge.
questions.explanation: To back into an alley, first drive past it and stop parallel to the edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking space.

questions.question: School buses:

options.text: Never have ABS.
Only have ABS if passengers under 10 years old will be on the bus.
May have ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have ABS.
questions.explanation: Most school buses made after 1998 or 1999 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS). Many older buses also have ABS.

questions.question: At a passive railroad crossing:

options.text: Each driver decides if it is safe to cross.
A control device tells you if it is safe to cross.
You should decide based on other vehicles around you.
Passengers decide if it is safe to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each driver decides if it is safe to cross.
questions.explanation: Passive railroad crossings have no traffic control devices. The driver must decide when it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must check all of the following, except:

options.text: The power steering belt.
The water compressor belt.
The alternator belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water compressor belt.
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip vehicle inspection test, you will check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts if the vehicle has them.

questions.question: When asked to change lanes during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Change lanes immediately without looking.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
Change lanes as fast as possible, even if you cut off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
questions.explanation: When the examiner asks you to change lanes, check your mirrors and blind spots, use your turn signal, and change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror of a school bus is used to:

options.text: Watch the passengers inside the bus.
See road hazards ahead.
See vehicles changing lanes.
See in front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the passengers inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror on a school bus lets you watch the passengers inside.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Parallel park.
Inspect your tires.
Monitor your gauges.
Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parallel park.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: If a bus stalls on railroad tracks, the driver should:

options.text: Get everyone off the bus and move far away from the tracks.
Keep everyone on the bus and try to signal the train to stop.
Keep everyone on the bus and wait for help.
Keep everyone on the bus and call a tow truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get everyone off the bus and move far away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If a school bus stalls on railroad tracks, get everyone off the bus right away. Lead students far away from the bus in the direction of any oncoming train. This protects them from flying debris if a train hits the bus.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you must check all of these EXCEPT:

options.text: The power steering belt.
The water pump belt.
The alternator belt.
The water compressor belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water compressor belt.
questions.explanation: Check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt. Look for cracks, frays, and tightness. There is no water compressor belt on vehicles.

questions.question: If the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working:

options.text: You will have no brakes.
You will still have brakes.
You should only use the parking brake to stop.
You should stop driving and wait for ABS to work again.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: ABS is an extra system that prevents wheels from locking during hard braking. If ABS fails, your regular brakes still work. You can drive and brake normally.

questions.question: When students board a bus, they should:

options.text: Sit in the back row first.
Sit in the back row only after all other seats are filled.
Sit as far from the driver as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit in the back row only after all other seats are filled.
questions.explanation: Do not use the back row unless the bus is full. Students are safer closer to the front in case of a rear-end crash. Students with special needs should sit near the driver.

questions.question: ABS helps you:

options.text: Lock up the wheels.
Keep the wheels from locking up.
Count the number of students boarding the bus.
Predict the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS stops the wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, which is an example of poor lane usage?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks
Stopping behind crosswalks
Driving in the left lane when more lanes are available
Finishing a right turn in the right lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in the left lane when more lanes are available
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane on multi-lane roads unless the lane is blocked. Do not cross curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines, crosswalks, and stop signs. Turn into the correct lane.

questions.question: During a bus evacuation, students should be led at least ____ away from the road.

options.text: 10 feet
20 feet
50 feet
100 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Lead students at least 100 feet away from the road in the direction of oncoming traffic. This keeps them safe from flying debris if another vehicle hits the bus.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Stop on the tracks.
Change gears.
Try to pass.
Stay in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: When crossing railroad tracks, do not stop, change gears, pass, or change lanes while your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.question: During the steering box inspection, you should NOT:

options.text: Check that the steering box is securely mounted.
Check that the steering box has no leaks.
Look for missing bolts in the steering box.
Assume all cotter keys are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are present.
questions.explanation: Check that the steering box is securely mounted. Look for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys. Make sure there are no power steering fluid leaks and the hoses are not damaged.

questions.question: When should a bus start moving after students have boarded?

options.text: As soon as the students are through the door
When the students are near their seats but still standing
When all students are seated and looking forward
As soon as the students cross the standee line

questions.correctAnswerText: When all students are seated and looking forward
questions.explanation: Wait until all students are seated and looking forward before moving the bus.
